papers.title: Effect of heat treatment regimes on microstructure and hardness of Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of various heat treatment regimes on the microstructure and hardness of Ti-6Al-4V alloy. By utilizing JMatPro software, the b-transus temperature, martensite start temperature, and phase constitution of the alloy were determined at various cooling rates of 0.1 °C/s, 30 °C/s, and 600 °C/s. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and optical microscopy (OM) were employed to characterize the specimens under different conditions: annealing, air cooling, quenching from b regime (1020 oC), dual-phase quenching (860 oC), and tempering at 600 oC. The lowest hardness (280 HV) was observed in the annealed sample, which exhibited a coarse-grained equilibrium microstructure. Upon quenching from 1020 oC, the prior b phase transforms entirely into acicular martensite with the hardness to 400 HV. Precipitation hardening induced by tempering at 600 oC leads to a significant increase in hardness, reaching a value of 539 HV. Furthermore, air cooling of the thin 2 mm specimen also promotes an ultra-fine basket-weave Widmanstätten and martensitic structure.
papers.venue: Journal of Science and Technology of Metal

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Ti-6Al-4V合金的热处理对显微组织和硬度的影响，但未明确针对增材制造材料，因此对AM后处理控制方向具有参考价值而非直接对应。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not explicitly study additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; its heat treatment regimes and hardness results are for conventionally processed material, missing the as-built microstructure and the link to fatigue or tensile performance of AM parts.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示不同热处理工艺对Ti-6Al-4V合金显微组织和硬度的影响规律
summary_zh.method: 通过JMatPro计算相变温度，结合XRD和光学显微镜表征退火、空冷、淬火及回火后的组织与硬度
summary_zh.result: 淬火获得针状马氏体（硬度400 HV），600℃回火析出强化使硬度升至539 HV，退火后粗晶组织硬度最低（280 HV）
summary_zh.validation: 实验采用XRD、光学显微镜及维氏硬度测试验证组织与性能关系

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to elucidate the effects of different heat treatment regimes on the microstructure and hardness of Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: JMatPro software was used to calculate phase transformation temperatures, and X-ray diffraction (XRD) and optical microscopy (OM) characterized specimens after annealing, air cooling, quenching, and tempering.
summary_en.result: Quenching produced acicular martensite (400 HV), tempering at 600°C induced precipitation hardening reaching 539 HV, while annealing resulted in coarse grains with the lowest hardness of 280 HV.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through experimental hardness measurements and microstructural characterization using XRD and OM.
